The H4 rule ('3-seed >=0.755 or two runs averaging >=0.7535') let in a tip whose true local mean sits on the 0.753 gate. A first draw of >=0.755 from a 0.7533 distribution happens about 13% of the time. The texts of H2, H4, H6.4.2, H6.5.1, H7.1.3 and H8.1.1 still quote 0.7548 and '~0.15 pp margin'. That refutes the launch-bound reading, but H2.4.2 is still 'open', the CUDA-graph and NS-overlap hypotheses are still open, and the H2 statement still lists per-step levers. E045's 282 W at 98% busy means low-occupancy small kernels, not idle gaps. E038's '~2 ms saved per removed step' is per-step GPU work (Muon NS and momentum, SGD foreach, lookahead), not launch overhead. H2.14.1 and H2.14.2 are also still 'open' even though E053 and E056 confirmed both time gains.

The levers there are less per-step GPU work (Muon's share, which the E052 profile can report directly; this also gates H7.2.4) or larger fused kernels. Make static shapes + max pool the default base code for every later experiment.

If 320 recovers >=80% of its FLOP share, a scored 320 run on the static/max-pool base becomes a reasonable FLOP-reducing lever, and FLOP cuts transfer best to the 300 W judge.

critiques.target: Untried direction: the Triton elementwise kernels (~30% of GPU time, E052)
critiques.issue: E052 found that the fused BN/GELU/elementwise Triton kernels take about 30% of GPU time in every phase. That is the largest measured cost block nobody has attacked, it is math-neutral, and it is memory-traffic and energy bound, so savings should transfer to the PCIe judge. All the effort went to Muon per-step costs and schedule cuts instead, even though E052 showed profiling finds real levers (the max-pool backward was ~4%).
critiques.suggestion: Untimed per-kernel breakdown: how many passes over each fp16 activation do BN stats, BN apply, GELU and their backward make? Then try compile-level options first (Inductor fusion and tuning flags, warmed in build). Next, try a hand-written fused BN-apply+GELU fwd/bwd Triton kernel for the 24/32 px shapes. Predict the time from the bytes moved before scoring.

critiques.target: H4.3 / H4.4: structure of the run-to-run variance
critiques.issue: The per-seed spreads show a pattern no Lvl1 hypothesis explains. E052's seeds were 0.7514-0.7521 and E056's 0.7511-0.7534, while E046's spanned 0.7523-0.7572. That looks like a per-run offset shared by all 3 trials. This fits cuDNN benchmark picks, which are cached once per process in build and reused across trials. If true, the 3 seeds give much less independent information than assumed. Some algorithm sets (e.g. lower-precision fp16 Winograd/FFT paths) might also cost accuracy systematically, which would make the pick an accuracy lever rather than pure noise.
critiques.suggestion: Untimed and cheap: log the cuDNN kernel names per conv shape in each run (from profiler kernel names) and correlate algorithm sets with the run mean over the next several runs. If a pick set tracks low accuracy, restrict the selection in build (e.g. benchmark_limit or a per-shape choice) without deterministic=True, which cost 9.8%. Add a Lvl1 or H4 child for 'run-level offset from algorithm choice'.

critiques.target: Provenance of reruns (E028, E048, E052) and the 'math-neutral' claims (E053, E056)
critiques.issue: E028's description says 'repeat E021' and E048/E052's say 'rerun E044', but the times (5.52, 4.97, 4.95 s) and the outcomes show E026/E046 code ran. The pooled-family estimate and the head-gain estimate both depend on which code actually ran. Separately, 'mathematically identical' max(dim).values vs AdaptiveMaxPool2d can still route gradients differently on fp16 ties. Static graphs may also pick different kernels. So E053/E056 are math-equivalent, not bit-equivalent, and pooling them into the family assumes no small bias.
critiques.suggestion: Diff commits e6c8e93, 4fd9ea5, 5a77f89 and 6262ecd against 2fda094 and record the result. From now on, log a hash of the submission source in each row. Untimed check: compare the pool's gradients on one fixed batch, old vs new. If they match except for ties, pooling E053/E056 is justified.

critiques.target: 'Closed' declarations (E034 Muon lr, E037 LS, E030 momentum, E033 NS, E049 head lr, E051 warmup)
critiques.issue: Each was closed by a single run, mostly on the bs-1024, head-on-SGD E026 base, and judged against a reference that was itself a lucky first draw. One run with sd 0.15 pp cannot detect the +0.15-0.2 pp the loop now needs (about 1.3 sd), so 'closed' really means 'no effect larger than about 0.3 pp on an older base'.
critiques.suggestion: Write the closures that way in the tree. For the remaining zero-cost accuracy probes, budget 2 runs per arm and prefer the ones with a mechanism tied to the ~256-step regime: Muon LR floor 0.05 (H6.5.1), a short final EMA, and freezing the whitening bias after ~20% of steps (Fable/hiverge). Run them only after the E049/E047 replicates, and stack them on the E056 base.

structured_output.summary:
The main problem is that the baseline is inflated. Five runs of the tip code average 0.7533 (sd 0.15 pp), not the 0.7548 that every recent verdict and the H2/H4/H6/H7/H8 texts use. E046 became the tip on a high draw, so the real local margin is about 0. Re-baselining changes several conclusions:
- **E051** (halved warmup) goes from "refuted" to noise. That removes the premise of H8.1.2 and most of H8's support.
- **E050** (width cut to 352) trades at the same rate as schedule trims.
- **E049** (head Muon lr 0.5x) is now +0.25 pp, the best zero-cost accuracy signal available.
- **E047** (2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32) matches E046's time with possibly higher accuracy, and it was discarded only because it was compared with a lucky draw.

E044's +0.32 pp head gain was never independently replicated. An indirect estimate puts it at about +0.15 pp.

E052 showed the GPU 98% busy at 16 px. That refutes the launch-bound story, so H2.4.2 should be refuted and H2.12.* retired. The H2.14 time levers are confirmed and still marked open. Static shapes plus the max(dim).values pool (-4.8%) should become the base code.

Untried directions with evidence behind them:
- Fused BN/GELU elementwise kernels, about 30% of GPU time.
- A per-layer profile before any more width cuts.

Not explained by any Lvl1 hypothesis:
- The per-run accuracy offsets shared across all 3 seeds (E052, E056). These are plausibly cuDNN algorithm picks cached once per process in build.
- Why E050 saved only half its estimated FLOP time.

Recommended next step: a 2x2 of head lr 0.5x × the E047 schedule on the E056 base, two runs per arm, with each arm judged against the pooled 0.7533. Also tighten the H4 promotion rule so the loop stops selecting for luck.
